sourceTitle: Bit Manipulation Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
title: Minimum Bit Flips
description: Return how many bits must be flipped to turn start into goal. That is the number of 1 bits in start XOR goal; clear the lowest set bit with x & (x - 1) until nothing is left.
referenceCode:
def min_bit_flips(start, goal):
    diff = start ^ goal
    flips = 0
    while diff:
        diff &= diff - 1
        flips += 1
    return flips

title: Single Number
description: Every value in nums appears twice except one. Return the one that appears once, using XOR so that the pairs cancel out.

title: Single Number II
description: Every value appears three times except one, which appears once. Return it in linear time and constant space. Track which bits have been seen once and twice.

title: Single Number III
description: Exactly two values appear once and every other value appears twice. Return the two values in ascending order. XOR everything, then split the values by the lowest bit where the two singles differ.

sourceTitle: Divide two numbers without multiplication and division
title: Divide Without Dividing
description: Return dividend / divisor truncated toward zero, without using multiplication, division or modulo. Subtract shifted copies of the divisor, largest first. If the result overflows a 32-bit signed integer, return 2147483647.

title: All Subsequences with Bitmasks
description: Every integer mask from 1 to 2^n - 1 picks a non-empty subsequence of s (bit i keeps s[i]). Return all of them sorted alphabetically. Subsequences built from different positions are listed separately even if equal.

sourceTitle: XOR of numbers in a given range
title: XOR of a Range
description: Return L xor (L + 1) xor ... xor R. The XOR of 1..n follows a cycle of four, so XOR(1..R) xor XOR(1..L - 1) answers it in constant time.

title: Assign Cookies
description: Child i is happy with a cookie of size at least greed[i], and each child gets at most one cookie. Return the most children you can make happy. Sort both lists and match greedily.

title: Lemonade Change
description: Lemonade costs 5. Customers pay in order with a 5, 10 or 20 bill and you start with no change. Return whether you can give every customer correct change. Prefer giving a 10 over two 5s.

title: Jump Game
description: From index i you may jump up to nums[i] steps forward. Starting at index 0, return whether you can reach the last index. Track the farthest index reachable so far.

title: Shortest Job First
description: All processes arrive at time 0 and run without interruption, shortest burst first. Return the average waiting time, rounded down to an integer.

title: Job Sequencing
description: Each job is [id, deadline, profit] and takes one unit of time; it earns its profit only if finished by its deadline, and only one job runs at a time. Return [jobs done, total profit] for the most profitable schedule. Take jobs by profit and put each in the latest free slot before its deadline.

title: Meetings in One Room
description: Meeting i runs from start[i] to end[i]. A meeting can follow another only if it starts strictly after the other ends. Return the most meetings one room can host. Pick by earliest end time.

title: Remove Overlapping Intervals
description: Return the fewest intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint do not overlap.

title: Insert an Interval
description: intervals is sorted by start and has no overlaps. Insert new_interval, merge anything it overlaps (touching counts as overlapping), and return the result.
referenceCode:
def insert_interval(intervals, new_interval):
    result = []
    begin, finish = new_interval
    index = 0
    while index < len(intervals) and intervals[index][1] < begin:
        result.append(intervals[index])
        index += 1
    while index < len(intervals) and intervals[index][0] <= finish:
        begin = min(begin, intervals[index][0])
        finish = max(finish, intervals[index][1])
        index += 1
    result.append([begin, finish])
    result.extend(intervals[index:])
    return result

sourceTitle: Minimum number of platforms required for a railway
title: Minimum Platforms
description: Train i arrives at arrival[i] and leaves at departure[i] (times written as HHMM). A train needs a platform for its whole stay, and a train arriving at the moment another departs still needs its own platform. Return the fewest platforms that avoid any waiting.
referenceCode:
def min_platforms(arrival, departure):
    arrival = sorted(arrival)
    departure = sorted(departure)
    i = j = 0
    platforms = best = 0
    while i < len(arrival):
        if arrival[i] <= departure[j]:
            platforms += 1
            best = max(best, platforms)
            i += 1
        else:
            platforms -= 1
            j += 1
    return best

title: Parentheses with Wildcards
description: s contains '(', ')' and '*'. Each '*' may act as '(', ')' or nothing. Return whether s can be read as balanced. Track the smallest and largest possible number of open brackets as you scan.

title: Candy
description: Children stand in a line with ratings. Every child gets at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour gets more candy than that neighbour. Return the fewest candies needed. Sweep left to right, then right to left.

sourceTitle: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
title: Points from Cards
description: Take exactly k cards, each from the left or right end of the row. Return the highest possible total. Equivalently, find the window of n - k cards with the smallest sum that you leave behind.
referenceCode:
def max_score(cards, k):
    total = sum(cards[:k])
    best = total
    for taken_right in range(1, k + 1):
        total += cards[-taken_right] - cards[k - taken_right]
        best = max(best, total)
    return best

title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
description: Return the length of the longest substring of s with no repeated character. Keep a window and each character's last position; jump the left edge past a repeat.

title: Longest Ones with K Flips
description: nums holds 0s and 1s. You may flip at most k zeros to ones. Return the length of the longest run of ones you can make. Grow a window and shrink it whenever it holds more than k zeros.

title: Fruit into Two Baskets
description: Walking right from any tree, you pick one fruit per tree but may carry only two kinds. Return the most fruit you can pick: the longest window containing at most two distinct values.

sourceTitle: Longest Substring With At Most K Distinct Characters
title: Longest Substring with K Distinct Letters
description: Return the length of the longest substring of s that contains at most k distinct characters.

title: Longest Repeat After K Replacements
description: You may replace at most k characters of s. Return the length of the longest substring of one repeated letter you can make. A window is valid while its length minus its most common letter's count is at most k.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t, counting duplicates. If several shortest windows exist, return the one that starts first. Return an empty string if no window works.

sourceTitle: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
title: Substrings with a, b and c
description: s contains only 'a', 'b' and 'c'. Return how many substrings contain at least one of each. For each right edge, every start at or before the earliest last-seen position works.
